title: The nested output reports the host's scale
body:
The nested output that decade advertises to its clients reports a scale of
1, set in `compositor::run` through `Output::change_current_state`. The
window decade itself lives in sits on a monitor Hyprland runs at 1.25, so
ghostty picks a scale of 1 and renders small, and its text is not crisp
where the host upscales it. The chrome has the same problem from the other
side: `Font::load` takes `FONT_PX` times the winit window's scale factor,
and that factor came back as 1 on the first frame, so the chrome drew 238
columns where 173 were expected.

## Proposal

Report the host's scale to clients and use it for the chrome.

- Read the scale from the winit window at start and on every
  `WinitEvent::Resized`, which carries `scale_factor`.
- Advertise it on the output. An integer scale goes through `wl_output`
  as `Scale::Integer`. A fractional one needs the fractional-scale and
  viewporter globals, which smithay has under `wayland::fractional_scale`
  and `wayland::viewporter`, with the output at `Scale::Fractional`.
- Size the pane in logical pixels when configuring a toplevel, and place
  client elements with the scale in `render_elements_from_surface_tree`.
- Rebuild the font, glyph cache and chrome texture when the scale changes.

## Open

- Whether to support only integer scales first. 1.25 is the monitor this is
  developed on, so fractional is the one that matters.
close_reason: Done at the commit titled 'Report the host's scale to clients' on dev, 2026-11-06. The output reports Scale::Fractional from the winit window's scale factor, fractional-scale and viewporter globals are offered, and ghostty renders at 1.25 in its pane with the chrome back at 173 columns on the 1920-wide dev output. Integer-only was not needed: fractional worked first.
